source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a loading regimen when rapid titration is desired, then continue an individualized maintenance regimen based on response and patient factors.","B":"Use a loading regimen to eliminate the need for maintenance therapy after the initial doses have produced the desired clinical response in the client.","C":"Use a loading regimen mainly to reduce digoxin toxicity because larger initial doses are safer than individualized maintenance dosing.","D":"Use a loading regimen so later monitoring is unnecessary once the initial doses have been tolerated and the client has reached the expected response."}}
source_row.rationale: Current digoxin labeling states that dosing may begin with a loading dose followed by maintenance dosing when rapid titration is desired. Option A is correct. Option B incorrectly eliminates maintenance therapy. Option C incorrectly presents loading as a strategy for reducing toxicity; dosing still requires careful individualization. Option D incorrectly removes the need for later assessment and monitoring.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Digoxin Tablets — Dosage and Administration §2.1 Important Dosing and Administration Information: when rapid titration is desired, initiate with a loading dose followed by maintenance dosing; dosing must be individualized using age, lean body weight, renal function, concomitant drugs, response, serum concentrations, and toxicity. FDA digoxin tablets label updated 2026-01-29; current DailyMed label live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A provider considers a digoxin loading regimen because rapid titration is desired. Which statement best explains the role of the loading regimen?
